newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: More N.Koreans escape to Hong Kong - reports.
newsitem.headline: More N.Koreans escape to Hong Kong - reports.

text.p: Two North Koreans, at least one an intelligence agent, have fled to Hong Kong where 17 other escapees sought refuge in the biggest mass defection from the communist nation, South Korean media reported on Sunday.
Officials for South Korea's Agency for National Security Planning could not confirm the reports which differed on whether both defectors were intelligence agents.

Yonhap News Agency quoted a Hong Kong public security source as identifying the two as Yu Bong-nam, a member of the North Korean Public Security Ministry, and Chon Hak-chol who it described as a North Korean intelligence agent.
However the Korea Broadcasting System said Chon was a North Korean student not an intelligence agent.

Yonhap said Yu, who arrived in Hong Kong in October, spied on North Korean students in Beijing while it said Chon was in charge of intelligence work against South Korea's Agency for National Security Planning in China. Chon fled to Hong Kong in November.
It said Yu was recalled to North Korea from Beijing after spying on North Korean students there in 1994. He was demoted and sent to serve in a rural area.
Unhappy with the demotion, Yu fled back to China and after spending five months there, was smuggled into Hong Kong.
Yonhap said Chon fled to Hong Kong when he believed his life was in danger because of errors he committed in his work in China.

South Korea had said on Thursday that 17 North Koreans -- 16 members of one family and a security guard -- had fled through China to Hong Kong in November and were now waiting for asylum in South Korea.
It was the biggest mass escape from North Korea since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War.
Yonhap said the latest two escapees brought to 35 the total number of North Koreans who have fled to Hong Kong to seek asylum in South Korea since 1993.

Officials from the Unification Ministry, which deals with inter-Korean matters, said on Friday South Korea would build its first camp next year to cope with a possible surge in defections from North Korea because of the Stalinist nation's deteriotraing economic condition.
The Koreas have been technically at war since the Korean War.
